newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end slightly up in lethargic trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end slightly up in lethargic trade.

text.p: Tokyo stocks ended lethargic trade slightly higher on Monday, in the aftermath of the turbulence in the New York stock market. Some investors bargain-hunted after sharp sell-offs in Tokyo last week, which made brokers expect trade to be range-bound for the rest of the year.
The key 225-issue Nikkei average was up 80.65 points, or 0.40 percent, to finish at 20,422.04. Its March futures added 110 points to 20,420.
"It was directionless trade, with nothing to trade on actively," said Tetsuya Ishijima, chief strategist at Okasan Securities Co Ltd.
Shares in non-life insurers sagged across the board, as settlement of the Japan-U.S. insurance dispute on Saturday sparked worries that the insurers would face fierce competition in the future.

Sumitomo Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd shares dropped 22 yen to close at 718 yen, Tokio Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd down 20 yen to end at 1,120 yen, and Mitsui Marine & Fire Insurance Co Ltd down 16 yen to close at 634 yen.
Shares in Yaohan Japan Corp rebounded to end up after the media reported its restructuring plans.
The reports said Yaohan would freeze plans to open 100 new supermarkets in Japan as a part of its restructuring measures.
The Yaohan retailing group later said in a statement that it would slim down its overseas operations.
The shares closed four yen up at 470 after early losing 19 yen to 447 yen.
The banking sector rebounded after falling prey to heavy selling in recent weeks. They said the rise was fuelled only by technical factors.
Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd rose 50 yen to close at 2,090.
